body.statement: Construct \(\widetilde\Psi_i\), \(\widehat\Gamma\), and \(G_n^*\) with the common total ridge convention \((\widehat H_c^{\mathrm{tot}})^{-1}\). Under the explicit uniform estimated-influence replacement condition \(\delta_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), the covariance estimator is uniformly consistent, \(\sup_{c,t\in\mathcal C}\|\widehat\Gamma(c,t)-\Gamma(c,t)\|\to_{\mathbb P}0\), and the conditional law of the stacked shared-multiplier process \(G_n^*\) given \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) converges in probability in bounded-Lipschitz distance on \(C(\mathcal C)^{d+4}\) to the law of \(G\). The event \(\mathcal E_n\) has probability tending to one and, on that event, the total ridge convention equals ordinary Hessian inversion simultaneously for every \(c\in\mathcal C\).
body.justification: One shared multiplier path preserves covariance across preferences and all stacked coordinates, while the product-bias, sum-radius, path plug-in, and softmax-entropy bounds make the fold-specific plug-in step auditable.
body.gap: BelloniChernozhukovChetverikovWei2018 validates estimated-score multipliers generically; the new theorem verifies its replacement and tightness requirements for the anchor's cross-fitted implicit optimizer path.
body.consumer: An applied researcher can compute one critical value without re-solving the policy optimization inside each bootstrap draw.
